transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (HeliosIQ Procurement), Ravi Shah (HeliosIQ InfoSec), Marta Lopez (HeliosIQ Engineering)

Summary:
Quick triage between procurement and security on DPA exceptions, finalize pricing route (annual commit vs usage + burst), confirm KMS/SSO requirements and next steps to get pilot signed off.

Topics:
- DPA exception list and redline path
- SLA commitments (uptime, p50/p95 latency targets)
- Billing model: committed annual vs committed monthly + burst pricing
- Key management (BYOK/HSM) and audit log retention
- Pilot scope and technical checkpoints

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick round of intros, I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, Samir our systems SE is here as well.
[00:12] Dana (HeliosIQ): Hi, Dana here, procurement. We have Ravi from security and Marta from engineering on call too.
[00:18] Samir (Redwood): Hi all. I think agenda was to triage a couple DPA exceptions and lock down pricing path for the pilot.
[00:26] Dana: Correct. Our legal / procurement asked for a fast read on what exceptions are live and whether you can accept our proposed data residency clause and extended audit retention.
[00:35] Alex: Totally. We pulled together a proposed DPA with three areas we usually flag: encryption keying, subprocessor list, and audit log retention. Samir, want to cover the technical constraints?
[00:45] Samir: Sure. For the BYOK request you raised — Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS and we have an HSM-backed option for Dedicated/private deployments. On hosted, we offer a KMS integration but there are some egress logging nuances; the logs are accessible but for full HSM custody you'd be looking at Dedicated or Private.
[00:59] Ravi: That nuance is game-changing for us. Our compliance team insists on HSM-backed keys with separation of duties and monthly key rotation logs. Are those logs available for export to our SIEM?
[01:09] Samir: Yes, logs can be exported. The export path is S3-compatible with encrypted transport; push to customer's bucket is supported. Small note: the field names in logs right now reflect internal naming — we can map them, but that mapping work is part of the pilot setup.
[01:26] Marta: When you say "push to our bucket" do you mean you store copies or you only forward events? We need to understand retention — our legal wants seven years, which is higher than your default.
[01:38] Alex: Seven years is outside of our standard offering. We typically retain audit logs for two years in hosted, and up to five years in Dedicated with a governance add-on. We'll need to flag that as an exception and map the cost/operational burden.
[01:52] Dana: Understood. Can we put that as a DPA exception request and you give us a price delta? Procurement prefers a single contract rather than tooling add-ons if possible.
[02:02] Alex: Yes, we can present options. We usually show two paths: 1) accept standard retention and a contractual SLA, or 2) bespoke retention for an additional fee and technical handoff to run the export pipeline. We'll quantify in the redline.
[02:16] Ravi: Next on SLA — your doc lists 99.9% and an SLO for p95 latency on standard chat calls. Our product team expects <120ms p50 for authentication related inference paths. Is that realistic on hosted?
[02:28] Samir: That's tight for hosted at peak concurrency, especially if you hit longer seq lengths. For p50 120ms we usually recommend Dedicated with GPU pinning and tuned batching. On hosted we can get close for typical profiles, but we can't guarantee it under bursty loads.
[02:42] Marta: Pinning and Dedicated means we commit to reserved capacity, right? How large is the minimum?
[02:48] Samir: We have bundle sizes. For the latency SLO you want, a small Dedicated pool (4 GPUs) with the right model variant and quantization profile is usually adequate. I can run a sizing estimate once you share expected QPS and token distribution.
[03:02] Dana: Procurement will need a firm unit price for the committed option and a separate burst rate. Can you provide an annual commit vs month-to-month comparison?
[03:11] Alex: Yes. We'll provide a rate-card: committed annual discounted rate, monthly committed, and a burst rate per 1k tokens above committed throughput. We'll also include a pilot-only rate so you can test before committing.
[03:23] Dana: Great. On the DPA redlines — our legal wants to add a clause for audit rights and third-party audits annually. How do you handle that?
[03:33] Alex: We accept third-party audits for Dedicated/Private under an enterprise agreement; for hosted we provide SOC 2 reports and can provide an attestation package. For annual third-party audits on our platform on your behalf, that's typically a custom addendum.
[03:47] Ravi: Also encryption-at-rest — standard AES-256 is fine but we need proof of key separation and periodic role-based access reports in the contract.
[03:56] Samir: We can provide role-based access control logs. The names/IDs in the logs may appear as internal service principals — we will map and produce a manifest. That mapping is typically an engineering effort during onboarding.
[04:09] Dana: Would that mapping be part of the standard onboarding or a billable service?
[04:14] Alex: For enterprise customers it can be included in onboarding up to a fixed scoping window (e.g., 40 hours). Anything beyond we quote. We'll note that in the redline.
[04:25] [05:00] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[04:58] Marta: I have a technical question — latency aside, how do you handle KV cache and multi-tenant prefix caching? We want to ensure inference consistency across sessions.
[05:10] Samir: Good question. Our runtime uses prefix-level KV caching; for Dedicated we can do namespace isolation so cache isn't shared across tenants. On hosted, cache is tenant-separated logically but we don't expose cache controls to customers. If you need deterministic cache behavior, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[05:26] Marta: So for the pilot, we should probably run on Dedicated to mirror production.
[05:31] Alex: Makes sense. We'll dimension the pilot to reflect production constraints.
[05:36] Dana: Back to pricing: procurement has an internal approval cut-off next Thursday, so if we can get pricing and the DPA redline by Wednesday we can queue it. Is that feasible?
[05:47] Alex: We can aim for that. I'll circulate a DPA with our standard positions and highlight the three exceptions: 1) 7-year log retention, 2) BYOK HSM proof obligations, and 3) annual third-party audit clause.
[05:59] Dana: Perfect. On the BYOK HSM — is that available on hosted with a partner KMS or only Dedicated/Private?
[06:08] Samir: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) where Redwood holds no copy of the key material; HSM-backed BYOK (with hardware key custody) is only fully supported on Dedicated/Private deployments where you can control physical keying or connect to your HSM via VPN.
[06:26] Ravi: We will need an architectural diagram showing where key material lives and where the logs flow. Can you include that in the security packet?
[06:34] Samir: Yes, I'll attach a diagram and a short runbook of key lifecycle events.
[06:38] Alex: We'll also include a sample SLA with p50/p95 numbers for both hosted and Dedicated, and an appendix describing fallback behavior if capacity is constrained.
[06:49] Dana: Talk to me about fallback — our product team will not accept silent degradations. We need clear fallbacks and a plan for model variant substitution.
[06:58] Samir: Redwood has a smart routing/fallback policy: requests can be routed by latency, cost, region, or a strict policy; we support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant and notification hooks. That behavior will be in the contract under the availability and graceful degradation clause.
[07:14] Marta: Are you able to guarantee no output quality regression if you fallback to a smaller model? We rely on specific prompt behaviors.
[07:22] Samir: We can't guarantee identical outputs across model families; what we do is include an A/B test and rollout policy so you can define which endpoints are allowed to fallback and which are strict. For the pilot we'll train against your test prompts and capture quality metrics.
[07:36] Dana: On billing — we need a sample invoice layout showing committed vs burst charges and any add-on fees for retention or mapping work.
[07:45] Alex: We'll provide that. The finance team typically shows invoicing by line item: base committed capacity, token usage overage, add-ons (log retention, mapping hours), and professional services.
[07:57] Ravi: Also include the KMS audit trail. That ties into our SOX obligations.
[08:03] Alex: Understood.
[08:06] [08:30] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[08:28] Dana: A little process note — if procurement gets the redlined DPA and pricing by Wednesday, I can route internally for a final sign-off to our CISO and CFO. After that, we want a 30-day pilot starting payments-on-commit for a small pool.
[08:42] Alex: Sounds good. We commonly do a 30-day pilot with a short payment or deposit and then convert to committed term if metrics meet your gates.
[08:52] Marta: What instruments are available for the onboarding pilot? Do you give a sandbox token or a dedicated cluster?
[08:59] Samir: For the pilot we can either spin up a small Dedicated cluster for deterministic testing or provide a scoped hosted environment with priority routing. Given your latency needs, I'd recommend the small Dedicated cluster.
[09:12] Dana: Okay we'll note that as preferred.
[09:17] Alex: Let's talk timelines: I'll aim to get the redline and rate-card by 2025-06-18. Samir will provide the pilot access and the security packet by 2025-06-19. Ravi, Dana — you'll review and flag any showstopper items.
[09:31] Ravi: One more ask — can you include in the packet a short section on vendor incident timelines (RTO/RPO) and breach notification commitments? Our legal needs specific hours.
[09:41] Samir: Yes, we have standard breach notification timelines in our playbook; we'll include an excerpt indicating notification within 72 hours and dedicated post-incident reports. We can negotiate shorter windows in an enterprise agreement.
[09:53] Dana: That should be explicit in the redline.
[09:57] Alex: Absolutely.
[10:00] [10:30] Speaker 1: (pause)
[10:27] Marta: Technical nit — do you support SAML 2.0 or only OIDC for SSO?
[10:31] Samir: Both. SAML and OIDC supported for SSO; provisioning via SCIM is available for Dedicated and Private.
[10:39] Marta: Good. We'll need a SCIM connector if we go Dedicated.
[10:44] Alex: Another procurement question — payment terms: net-30 is standard; we can discuss net-45/60 for Enterprise with committed spend. Any constraints?
[10:55] Dana: Net-30 preferred; CFO may negotiate net-45 depending on commitment size. We'll flag after pricing.
[11:03] Alex: Okay.
[11:05] [11:40] Speaker 4: (background noise)
[11:38] Dana: Any competitor considerations — our engineering team mentioned InferenceCorp pitched on-prem with a big discount but lacked autoscaling and caching features. Do you have a doc comparing hosted vs on-prem tradeoffs?
[11:53] Samir: Yes, we have a short TCO playbook that compares Hosted/Dedicated/Private, latency and ops tradeoffs, and the unit economics. I'll attach that.
[12:02] Dana: Please do.
[12:05] Alex: Quick recap for next steps: (1) Redwood sends DPA redline and pricing worksheet by 2025-06-18; (2) Redwood SE sends security packet, architectural diagram, and pilot access window by 2025-06-19; (3) HeliosIQ confirms internal approvers and final decision timeline by 2025-06-17.
[12:25] Dana: That's accurate.
[12:27] Ravi: We'll also mark the audit log and retention ask as priority and get you the retention spec by 2025-06-20.
[12:35] Alex: Great. Any other questions?
[12:39] Marta: One request — can you run a quick throughput bench with our representative prompt set? If you can include that as part of the pilot report that'd be helpful.
[12:47] Samir: Yes, send the prompt set and we'll run the throughput/latency bench and include token-level cost breakdown.
[12:55] Alex: Ok going to wrap. Thanks everyone for time. We'll follow up with the materials and the redline.
[13:02] Dana: Thanks.
[13:04] Ravi: Thanks all.

End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription cut some proper nouns (KMS sometimes transcribed as K M S), occasional speaker attribution swapped during crosstalk.
